deep.reconstruction:
This page continues a numbered list of research questions (items 11-15; items 1-10 are on the previous page). The vocabulary points to the period of Pursuing Stacks, around 1983, not 1973. Terms such as test category, modelizer, W-aspheric, contracteur and homotopisme belong to that period. The 4 Jan 1973 letterhead on the reused typescript only gives a date before which the notes cannot have been written.

Item 11. Grothendieck seeks to characterise 'fibrations' in Cat. He means functors p: X' -> X such that base change along p carries weak equivalences (nerve-weak equivalences, or more generally those of a basic localizer W) to weak equivalences. In modern terms these are homotopy-pullback-stable maps: Rezk's 'sharp maps', the Cat analogue of quasifibrations, or 'W-smooth/proper'-type conditions.
- He first reduces the condition (the margin shows a tower of pullbacks Z'->Z, Y'->Y, X'->X). It should suffice to check base changes along Y -> X where Y has a final object y, and specifically the inclusion of the point {y} = e_y -> Y. That inclusion is a weak equivalence because Y is contractible.
- So the condition becomes: for every Y -> X with Y having a final object, the fibre of X' over y includes into X' x_X Y by a weak equivalence. This is a Quillen Theorem B / 'fibre = homotopy fibre' condition.
- He then asks whether it is enough to test only on composites Delta_0 -> Delta_n -> X, i.e. points of simplices [n] -> X. This is the Cat analogue of Rezk's criterion that sharpness can be tested over simplices.

Item 12. He proposes adding a new axiom to Quillen's model-category axiomatics. Given a cartesian square with f a fibration and g in W, the base change g' should be in W. This is exactly right properness, named by Bousfield-Friedlander in 1978. Item 11 is its 'intrinsic' version in Cat, where no fibrations are given and one defines them by the pullback property.

Item 13. He asks whether a 0-connected topos (perhaps one also satisfying a further hypothesis, illegible) is 'totally 0-connected'. That would mean pi_0 / the left adjoint of the inverse image preserves finite limits, in the Barr-Pare / Johnstone sense. He asks whether it suffices that the product of two connected objects is connected. He also states a homotopical variant: is it enough that the product of two W-aspheric objects is W-aspheric? This parallels the notion of a 'totally aspheric' test category in Pursuing Stacks.

Item 14. 'Homs in (Hot) and diagrams, variants', i.e. internal Hom / diagram categories of homotopy types. This is a derivator-type theme.

Item 15. A 'relatively ...' topos defined by a diagram over B, i.e. a relative/fibred topos given by a diagram over a base. It leads into the next page: cointegration on a topos, and a spectral sequence relating the homotopy of R-integral of a relative homotopy type to R^i f_* of its homotopy sheaves.
errors: No outright errors; these are questions.

Item 11's reduction to base changes e_y -> Y (Y with final object) is stated without proof. It requires the class of maps to be closed under the relevant composites and the pullback tower argument in the margin. It is plausible for a basic localizer (via Quillen's Theorem A / homotopy colimit decomposition of Y -> X over X/x). However, the passage from arbitrary weak equivalences to inclusions of final objects needs some localizer axioms.

Item 13: requiring only that binary products of connected objects be connected addresses preservation of finite products by pi_0, not of equalizers. Without further hypotheses this is a priori weaker than 'totally connected' (preservation of finite limits), so the hoped-for implication is not automatic.

ideas.what: Characterise functors in Cat whose base change preserves weak equivalences; reduce to base change along final-object inclusions; ask whether testing over simplices Delta_0 -> Delta_n -> X suffices
ideas.modern_name: sharp maps / homotopy-pullback-stable maps (quasifibrations in Cat); Quillen Theorem B condition
ideas.usually_credited_to: Rezk (sharp maps, 1998); Quillen (Theorem B, 1973); Cisinski / Maltsiniotis for Cat/localizer versions
ideas.where_published: Related smooth/proper-functor discussions in Pursuing Stacks and Les Dérivateurs (as presented by Maltsiniotis, Astérisque 301); exact statement unsure

ideas.what: Add to Quillen's axioms: pullback of a weak equivalence along a fibration is a weak equivalence
ideas.usually_credited_to: Bousfield-Friedlander (1978); property noted earlier for sSet by Quillen

ideas.what: Does connectedness of binary products of connected objects make a connected topos totally connected? Homotopical analogue for W-aspheric objects

missed.claim: Explicit question: can functors in Cat whose base change preserves weak equivalences be detected by testing only over Delta_0 -> Delta_n -> X? This is a Cat-internal analogue of Rezk's simplex criterion for sharp maps. I do not know a clean published statement of this for Cat with an arbitrary basic localizer.
missed.quote: Est-il suffisant que ce le soit pour tout Δ0 → Δn → X ?
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Testing over simplices would give a combinatorial criterion for homotopy-pullback-stable functors in Cat and for W-local versions (relevant to Cisinski-Maltsiniotis localizer theory). It may already be implied by known results; a specialist could settle it quickly.

missed.claim: Grothendieck sets side by side 'product of connected objects connected implies totally connected topos' and 'product of W-aspheric objects W-aspheric'. This links topos-theoretic total connectedness to his totally aspheric test categories, the same pattern later central to Lawvere's cohesion (pi_0 preserving finite products) and Johnstone's analysis.
missed.quote: Is it enough that product of two 0-connected objects is 0-connected (or of 2/W-aspheric objects is W-aspheric)?
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Only a mild anticipation. The homotopical side matches known Pursuing Stacks notions and the topos side was later treated by Johnstone and Lawvere, so this is not a substantial missed result.

deep.surprise_reason: A list of questions. Right properness (item 12) was standard by the likely date (~1983). Item 11 is a natural Theorem-B/sharp-map question, and item 13 anticipates themes later developed by Johnstone and Lawvere. Nothing finished or clearly absent from the literature.
